text:
Sam: heads up — noticed ~30% packet loss between pods in namespace gpu-prod during a large training batch, looks east-west across az-b -> az-c. RPCs timing out and worker restarts.

infra-bot: [alert] netpol-change detected on namespace=gpu-prod by infra-policy-sync (2024-06-15T15:22:18Z)

Maria: can you repro and paste the ping from a pod? which nodes/azs?

Sam: quick repro from bastion into pod, ping to another pod in same ns:
```
# from bastion
kubectl exec -n gpu-prod -c sidecar gpu-worker-12 -- ping -c 40 gpu-worker-34.gpu-prod.svc.cluster.local
---
40 packets transmitted, 28 received, 30% packet loss, rtt min/avg/max = 0.6/18.9/120 ms
```

Alex: that infra-bot entry suggests a policy was pushed. any recent netpol commits?

Jordan: running `kubectl get networkpolicy -n gpu-prod -o yaml` now. Found a policy named `namespace-lockdown` that looks like a blanket egress deny (empty egress list).

Sam: paste of the policy snippet we found:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: namespace-lockdown
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

Maria: that's a namespace-wide egress deny (podSelector empty + no allowed egress). That will block intra-namespace traffic unless there are explicit allow rules. How did that end up in gpu-prod? it should be scoped to infra/system namespaces only.

Alex: audit shows `infra-policy-sync` applied `ci:configs/netpols/lockdown.yaml` at 15:21 from pipeline run 9845. It looks like the sync job doesn't currently gate against deploying empty egress to app namespaces.

Jordan: aside — some gpu nodes are on instances with jumbo frames/RDMA enabled. I tcpdump'd on node A and saw ICMP fragmentation-needed plus some asymmetric replies; wonder if masquerade/mtu differences between azs made fragments fail when combined with policy drops.

Sam: saw similar in packet captures: a lot of fragmented UDP and ICMP fragmentation-needed responses from the node. Could be MTU mismatch + netpol forcing different routing on the return path.

Maria: quick mitigation — add a temporary allow rule for intra-namespace east-west and kube-system sidecars. Patch to apply now:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-internal-e2e-temp
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: gpu-prod
    - podSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
    - protocol: UDP
```

Alex: applied the temporary allow. infra-bot: policy sync shows namespace updated. Can someone smoke test?

Sam: reran the ping after the patch:
```
40 packets transmitted, 40 received, 0% packet loss, rtt min/avg/max = 0.5/1.1/2.8 ms
```

Jordan: confirmed application-level RPCs recovered for the training job. So the policy was the immediate cause. Still want to follow up on the MTU/masquerade observation for RDMA-enabled nodes — file a follow-up runbook item.

Maria: opened PR to config repo to scope the lockdown policy to `system-infra` namespace only and added a validation check in the sync pipeline to reject `egress: []` for non-system namespaces. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/repo/configs/pull/512

Alex: can we add an alert in infra-monitoring that triggers when a NetworkPolicy with `podSelector: {}` and empty `egress` is added to any namespace not labeled `system-infra` or `infra`? would have caught this earlier.

Jordan: adding to infra board and creating a short postmortem note: impact = 3 batch jobs failed, ~15m disruption to GPU queue, some pod restarts. attaching pcap and kube audit logs to the PM.

Sam: leaving the temporary allow rule in place until PR merges and the sync job is updated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
